1  COMPETENT AUTHORITY, GAIL (INDIA) LIMITED

THIS OP (CIVIL) HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 19.07.2022, THE COURT ON 09.10.2024 DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2 O.P.(C) NO.1292 OF 2022  2024:KER:74812  JUDGMENT (Dated: 9th October, 2024)
The 1st respondent is the owner in possession of 20 Ares 22 sq. meters (50 cents) of land in Re.Sy. No.365/9 of Thrikkakara North Village.

An extent of 13.74 cents of the said land was acquired under the Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of Users in Land) Act, 1962 (for short, 'PMP Act'), for laying the pipeline for the KKBMPL project.

entities.text: Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of Users in Land) Act, 1962
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The 2nd respondent was awarded a compensation of Rs.1,18,500/- to the 1st respondent.

Aggrieved by the fixing of the compensation, the 1st respondent filed Ext.P1 petition under Section 10(2) and (5) of the Petroleum and Mineral Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962 read with Rule 5 of the Petroleum (Acquisition of the User of Land) Rules, 1963 before the District Court,
Ernakulam, and numbered as OP(PMP) No.773 of 2015.

entities.text: Petroleum and Mineral Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Petroleum (Acquisition of the User of Land) Rules, 1963
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner filed a written statement controverting the allegations in O.P.(C) NO.1292 OF 2022 2024:KER:74812 the original petition.
Though several grounds were taken, including the Law Of Limitation, the District Court, by Ext.P3 order, enhanced the compensation.
2. The petitioner filed a Review Petition as R.P. No.10 of 2021 to review the order dated 24.02.2021.
The said R.P. was dismissed as per Ext.P4 order.
Challenging Exts.P3 and P4, the petitioner has filed this Original Petition before this Court under Article 227 of the Constitution of India.
3. The main ground raised by the counsel for the petitioner is that the learned District Judge has granted the compensation relying on G.O.(Rt) No.5165/2017/RD dated 01.12.2017.

As per Section 10 (4) of the Act, where the right of user of any land has vested in the Central Government, the State Government or the corporation, the Central Government, the State Government or the corporation,
as the case may be, shall, in addition to the compensation, if any, payable under O.P.(C) NO.1292 OF 2022 2024:KER:74812 sub-section (1), be liable to pay to the owner and to any other person whose right of enjoyment in that land has been affected in any manner whatsoever by reason of such vesting, compensation calculated at ten percent of the market value of that land on the date of the notification under sub-section (1) of section 3.

The learned District Judge has found that the fair value of the land is Rs.3,50,000/- and as per G.O(P) No.188/14 the Government has increased 50%
in fair value.
The market value per Are is Rs.3,50,000/- + 1,75,000/- i.e., Rs.5,25,000/-.

However,
taking note of G.O.(Rt) No.5165/2017/RD, 10 times the notified value was taken in fixing the compensation.

The petitioner is aggrieved by taking the value by 10 times, as the said Government Order was issued only on 01.12.2017, and it specifically states that the said Government Order is applicable for compensations for land taken from January 2012 onwards.

The counsel for the petitioner relied on the judgment of this O.P.(C) NO.1292 OF 2022 2024:KER:74812 Court in Sudhakaran Nayar T. v. State of Kerala and Others (2022 (3) KHC 539),
wherein the person whose land acquired under Phase I is not entitled to the benefit of G.O.(Rt)No.5165/2017/RD dated 01.12.2017.

entities.text: Sudhakaran Nayar T. v. State of Kerala and Others (2022 (3) KHC 539)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court held that there is no discrimination between the compensation granted to the land owners in Phase I and Phase II, as no person in Phase I had given the benefit of the said Government Order.

5. The counsel for the respondent argues that a reading of Ext.P1 petition would show that he had claimed compensation at the rate of Rs.5 lakhs per cent for the land acquired and compensation of Rs.68,70,000/- with interest at the rate of 12%.

He filed a proof affidavit before the District Court,
wherein, in paragraph 5, it is stated that at the time of Section 3(1) notification, the vested land had fetched Rs.5,00,000/- per cent.
However, the competent authority has fixed only a meager amount towards compensation.
The opposite O.P.(C) NO.1292 OF 2022 2024:KER:74812 party ought to have compensated for the true losses suffered.
As per Gazette Notification G.O.(Rt.) No.5165/2017 dated 1.12.2017, the claimant has the right to get 10 times the notified fair value of the property acquired.
The respondent claimed an amount of Rs.68,70,000/-.
Thus, the respondent has specifically claimed that he is entitled to the benefit of G.O.(Rt.) No.5165/2017 dated 1.12.2017.

In G.O.(Rt.) No.5165/2017, the Clauses I to VI reads as follows:
I. The market value for the purpose of computing land compensation under Section 10(4) of the Petroleum and Mineral Pipelines Act, 1962 shall be taken as 10 times the notified fair value of the land.
II. An ex gratia amount of Rs.5 lakhs shall be paid in respect of land holdings of less than 10 cents in extent through which the pipeline passes in case the landowner does not have any other property.

III. In respect of paddy lands through which the pipeline O.P.(C) NO.1292 OF 2022 2024:KER:74812 passes, a one time compensation in addition to the land compensation of Rs.3761 per cent shall be paid.
IV. Compensation at the above rates shall be payable in respect of all property through which the GAIL Pipeline passes in Kerala right from the beginning of construction activity in January, 2012.
V. The width of the ROU shall be two meters in respect of land holdings of less than 10 cents in extent through which the pipe line passes.
VI. A sketch authenticated by the Competent Authority showing the ROU required for GAIL shall be given to land owners of plots through which the pipeline passes.
No NOC from GAIL shall be required for utilizing land outside the ROU area demarcated in the sketch.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As per Clause No.4 of the said G.O., if the construction activities are done after January 2012,
they are entitled to 10 times the notified fair value of the land.
But the learned Judge simply accepted G.O.(Rt.)No.5165/2017, without evidence that the construction activities started after January 2012. O.P.(C) NO.1292 OF 2022 2024:KER:74812 7.
The counsel for the respondent also submits that he was not cross-examined on this point.
If the Government Order dated 1.12.2017 is applicable, then he is entitled to 10 times the notified fair value, and 10% of that amount shall be taken as the land value for fixing compensation.
This is the matter for evidence.
In the proof affidavit, the respondent has specifically stated that he is entitled to the benefit of G.O.(Rt.)No.5165/2017, but no evidence was adduced.
The Court below did not go into the said aspect.
Therefore, I am of the considered opinion that the question as to the applicability of G.O.(Rt.) No.5165/2017, as per the petitioner's case is concerned requires reconsideration.
In the result, Exts.P3 and P4 are set aside and it is remanded to the Additional District Judge for fresh consideration.
As far as the compensation with respect to other points is concerned, the same has now become final since it has not been challenged by the claimant. O.P.(C) NO.1292 OF 2022 2024:KER:74812
Therefore, the only question to be considered is the fixing of compensation based on the evidence available and whether G.O.(Rt.) No.5165/2017 is applicable or not.
The petitioner as well as the respondent/claimant, shall be given an opportunity to adduce further evidence.
Learned District Judge is directed to dispose of the case as expeditiously as possible within a period of six months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of the judgment.
